\chapter{Return to Believing and Changing}
\label{ch:pa-believe-change-r4}
\hlchaptermodality{167}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can retrieve two already-taught Punjabi action verbs after a long gap, one at a time, without claiming scored A1 writing or complete mock credit.}

Recall believing and changing from short familiar cues without introducing new Punjabi.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਮੰਨਣਾ} (mannṇā)}{ਮੰਨਣਾ (mannṇā)}]{An old word for believing}

\label{lesson:PA-R167-believe-again}



\begin{quote}
Hear \textbf{to believe, to agree}. Recall \textbf{\pa{ਮੰਨਣਾ}} (\emph{mannṇā}).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear \textbf{\pa{ਮੰਨਣਾ}}. Recall \textbf{to believe, to agree}. Then hear the English cue again. Say \textbf{\pa{ਮੰਨਣਾ}} before the model. Only this old word is needed.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
One last cue: \textbf{to believe, to agree}. Recall \textbf{\pa{ਮੰਨਣਾ}}. Listen and retry once if it does not come back.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਬਦਲਣਾ} (badalṇā)}{ਬਦਲਣਾ (badalṇā)}]{An old word for changing}

\label{lesson:PA-R167-change-again}



\begin{quote}
Hear \textbf{to change}. Recall \textbf{\pa{ਬਦਲਣਾ}} (\emph{badalṇā}).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Pause after each familiar meaning, then hear its model:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{to change} — \textbf{\pa{ਬਦਲਣਾ}} (\emph{badalṇā}).
  \item \textbf{to believe, to agree} — \textbf{\pa{ਮੰਨਣਾ}} (\emph{mannṇā}).
\end{itemize}

Only the order of these old words has changed.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Hear \textbf{to believe, to agree}, then \textbf{to change}. Pause after each cue and recall its Punjabi word before the model: \textbf{\pa{ਮੰਨਣਾ}}, \textbf{\pa{ਬਦਲਣਾ}}. Revisit only the old word you missed.
\end{tcolorbox}
